description: §18.5 — a block arm whose TAIL is a member/index-assignment statement (`{ …; o.n = 2 }`) yields VOID, and this decision is IDENTICAL across all three block-arm tail lowering positions: the raw-string path (literal-arm `1 :> { }` via emit-logic.ts _blockTailIsValueExpr), the structuredBody IIFE path (`.Variant :> { }` return position via emit-control-flow.ts emitMatchExpr), and the structuredBody tilde path (`.Variant :> { }` derived cell via emit-logic.ts emitMatchExprToTilde). Pre-fix the two _blockTailIsValueExpr-fed positions LIFTED the space-normalized `o . n = 2` as a chained assignment (raw-void and derived-void rendered "2") while the IIFE path VOIDED it (struct-void empty) — a source-identical arm with three-way-divergent meaning. This case is the differential: on base raw-void="2", derived-void="2", struct-void=""; post-fix all three are empty (void), while the value-tail controls (member READ `o.n`) all lift to "9".
rationale: §18.5: a block arm `{ statement* expression? }` yields its LAST expression; a block whose tail is a decl/assignment/lift/fail statement (or is empty) yields void. A member/index-assignment (`o.n = 2`, `xs[0] = 9`) is a statement, so its arm is void — the assigned value SHALL NOT become the arm result. The rule is ONE classifier (_blockTailIsValueExpr), so every lowering position makes the same call: the void arm renders nothing; a value tail (member READ `o.n`) lifts unchanged.
